title: StrategyStateChanged.v1
description: A strategy version moved through the governance lifecycle (A§60, plan §6.5 catalogue extension). Emitted by strategy-service on EVERY transition — including the ones that never reach production, such as SIMULATED→REJECTED — on `collections.strategy` keyed by `strategyId`, in the same transaction as the append-only `strategy_transition` row. The lifecycle is exactly A§60: DRAFT → TEST → SIMULATED → BUSINESS_APPROVED → RISK_APPROVED → SCHEDULED → ACTIVE → RETIRED, with SIMULATED and BUSINESS_APPROVED also able to go to REJECTED. The invariants the transitions enforce (DEC-3) are: TEST requires every ref to resolve; SIMULATED is system-only and requires a completed simulation for the current `contentHash`; the definition is frozen at TEST→SIMULATED; BUSINESS_APPROVED requires an approver who is not the author; SCHEDULED requires `effectiveFrom` today or later. This event is the notification, not the record — the record is the transition row.

strategyId.description: Identifier of the strategy family, e.g. `EARLY_COLLECTION`. Also the partition key, so one strategy's transitions arrive in order and a consumer never sees ACTIVE before RISK_APPROVED.

fromState.description: State the version was in, or NULL for the creation of version 1 of a new strategy (which has no prior state). Required and nullable rather than omitted: "created" and "transitioned from somewhere" must be distinguishable without inferring meaning from an absent key.

toState.description: State the version is now in.

actor.description: Who caused the transition: the identity provider `sub` of the human, or `system:<component>` for machine transitions (`system:strategy-scheduler` for a scheduled activation, `system:simulation` for TEST→SIMULATED). Four-eyes rules are checked against this identity — DEC-3 rejects an approval whose actor is the author with 403 — so it is a stable id, never a display name.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical JSON of the version's definition at the moment of the transition. Frozen from TEST→SIMULATED onward, so comparing the hash on the SIMULATED event with the hash on the ACTIVE event proves that nothing was edited between simulation, approval and activation. A mismatch against a recorded simulation is what makes TEST→SIMULATED fail after a definition edit.

state.title: StrategyState
state.description: The nine governance states of A§60, exactly. REJECTED is terminal for that version (clone it to try again) and so is RETIRED.
